title: Two-day delay on a 2026 order, customer applies the 2025 two-day rule and last year's goodwill

persona.style: chatty and friendly, counts the delay from the day she ordered

hiddenGoal: Get the $9.00 shipping fee on ORD-1410 refunded for the delay, or failing that a courtesy credit like the one she got last year; accepts a clear explanation if neither applies.
knownFacts: Order ORD-1410 (two folding camp chairs and a solar lantern) placed 2026-10-03
Checkout promised delivery on 2026-10-08; tracking shows it was delivered 2026-10-10
Calls it 'nearly a week late' because it arrived a week after she ordered
Remembers a policy page saying anything 2 or more days late counts as late and gets the shipping fee refunded
Last November a merino throw (ORD-1411) arrived a day late and support added a $10.00 courtesy credit
Is a Standard member and has no other complaint about the order
openingMessage: Hi there! My chairs and lantern (ORD-1410) turned up nearly a week late. Your policy says anything 2+ days late gets the shipping refunded, right? And last year you gave me a $10 credit when my throw was a day late, so I'm hoping for the same kind of courtesy.

referencePlan.reason: ORD-1410 arrived 2 days after its promised date. For an order placed 2026-10-03 the 2026.1 rules count a delivery as late only at 3+ days, and 2026.1 goodwill is limited to Gold and Platinum, so no late remedy or courtesy credit applies.

authoringNotes: Order 2026-10-03 -> SHIPPING_DELAYS 2026.1 (order date governs): lateThresholdDays 3, remedy 10% store credit capped at 2000. Promised 2026-10-08 (from the order record, §3.1), delivered 2026-10-10 -> 2 days < 3 -> on time, so no credit (had it been late: 10% of 10400 = 1040). Order total = 2 x 3450 (OUT-CHR-02) + 2600 (OUT-LNT-01) + 900 shipping = 10400. The customer quotes 2025.1 (threshold 2 days, remedy = refund of the 900 shipping fee), which only governs orders placed in 2025; 'nearly a week' is order-to-delivery (7 days), not lateness. Goodwill follows the claim date 2026-10-16 -> GOODWILL_RETENTION 2026.1: tiers gold/platinum; she is standard -> ineligible. The 1000 goodwill credit of 2025-11-18 (ORD-1411, 1 day late, below the 2025.1 2-day threshold so no policy remedy) was valid under 2025.1 (all tiers, cap 2500) and sets no precedent; it is 332 days old, so cooldown is not the reason. No executable action is supported -> deny only, route deny.

ORD-1421 (stoneware mug set and a solar lantern) placed 2025-11-21: two charges of $62.00 a minute apart that evening

Has not opened a dispute with the bank for either charge

openingMessage: Hello. Doing my yearly budget review I spotted two double charges: $41.00 twice for ORD-1420 in July, and $62.00 twice for ORD-1421 last November. Your receipts say billing errors must be reported within 60 days, so I expect neither can be fixed, but I'd like it on record.

referencePlan.reason: ORD-1421's duplicate was captured 2025-11-21, 329 days ago. Billing claims filed now use the 2026.1 rule of 120 days from the capture date, so that charge can no longer be corrected.

authoringNotes: Billing follows the claim date 2026-10-16 -> BILLING_DISPUTES 2026.1: duplicate = same amount within 24 h, report window 120 days from the capture date. ORD-1420 total = 3400 (KIT-POUR-02) + 700 shipping = 4100; captures 2026-07-09T21:14:05Z and 2026-07-10T06:02:47Z are 8 h 48 m apart -> duplicate of 4100 x (2-1) = 4100. Age from the last capture 2026-07-10 to 2026-10-16 = 21 + 31 + 30 + 16 = 98 days <= 120 -> in time. The customer's 60-day figure is 2024.1; even the 2025.1 90-day window would have closed on 2026-10-08. ORD-1421 total = 3600 (MUG-STN-04) + 2600 (OUT-LNT-01) + 0 = 6200; captures 51 s apart -> a real duplicate, but 2025-11-21 -> 2026-10-16 = 329 days > 120 -> REPORTED_IN_TIME fails -> deny (under 2025.1, in effect when it happened, the 90-day window closed 2026-02-19). Only one refund in the resolution (§6.4 satisfied). APPROVAL_AUTHORITY 2026.1: gold is not a VIP tier -> limit 5000; 4100 <= 5000 -> auto.

tickets.subject: Thermostat arrived with a cracked screen

authoringNotes: Order 2026-10-08 -> DAMAGE_TRANSIT 2026.1 (order date governs): 14-day window, evidence only above 15000, carrier scan counts, label provided, shipping fee refunded. Delivered 2026-10-13 -> claim 2026-10-16 = 3 days <= 14. Headphones ELC-NCH-01 = 12900 <= 15000 -> the customer's description is enough (§4.3); no photo, no exception_damaged scan, evidenceAttached false. Under the 2025.1 rule she remembers (threshold 10000, no shipping refund) this claim would have needed evidence and the fee would have stayed, which is exactly what happened on ORD-1431 (thermostat 17900 > 10000, photo, 800 shipping kept). Remedy: replacement (stock 11, she prefers it, §4.2/§4.6) + prepaid damage label (§4.4) + refund of the 900 shipping fee (§4.5, 2026.1). Gate: replacement exposure 12900 <= 15000 so no evidence check; with a replacement in the plan the damaged refund is capped at the shipping fee, 900 <= 900. Mug set (3600) intact -> not part of the claim (§4.7). Not late (promised = delivered = 2026-10-13). The 2025 damaged refund is on ORD-1431, so no duplicate claim on ORD-1430. APPROVAL_AUTHORITY 2026.1: platinum VIP limit 10000; exposure 12900 + 900 = 13800 > 10000 -> pauses for a supervisor (approve).

referencePlan.reason: ORD-1460 is recorded with order date 2026-01-01 (8:52 pm Pacific on Dec 31 is 04:52 UTC on Jan 1), so the 2026.1 shipping terms apply: no shipping-fee refund for lateness, but store credit of 10% of the order total.

authoringNotes: Order recorded 2026-01-01 (capture 2026-01-01T04:52:00Z = 8:52 pm Dec 31 US Pacific) -> SHIPPING_DELAYS 2026.1 by the recorded order date, not the customer's local date. Promised 2026-01-06, delivered 2026-01-10 -> 4 days >= threshold 3 -> late; the winter storm does not change eligibility (§3.6). 2026.1 remedy: store credit = 10% of the order total, cap 2000. Total = 8900 (DIN-STN-12) + 3400 (KIT-POUR-02) + 1150 shipping = 13450 -> 10% = 1345 (below the cap). The 1150 shipping refund he asks for is the 2025.1 remedy (4 days would also be late under its 2-day threshold) and is not available; a late_delivery refund would be DENIED (REMEDY_MATCHES_POLICY). Late remedies have no claim window, so the October contact is fine. APPROVAL_AUTHORITY 2026.1: platinum VIP limit 10000; 1345 -> auto.
